task.title: Float figures and wrap text around them
task.shortdesc: A float leaves the flow of the text and goes to an edge: the start or the end of its lines, the top or the bottom of the page, or of a column. The text goes on in the room the float leaves, around its shape if you give it one. The floats reference lists the properties used here.

context.p: The element names in the examples, such as figure, are placeholders. Use the names that occur in your XML.

step.cmd: Float a box beside its lines

info.p: Set float on an element. Its box goes to one side of the lines, and the text wraps on the other side for the height of the box. left and right are the two sides of the line. inline-start and inline-end are where the lines start and end, which follows the direction of the text: inline-start is the right in Hebrew or Arabic. block-start and top behave like inline-start here, and block-end and bottom like inline-end.

step.cmd: Start a box below the floats

info.p: Set clear on a block to start it below the earlier floats on the sides you name. both clears both sides. A value that names the start side, such as left in a text that runs from left to right, also starts the block below an initial letter.

image.alt: A box with a float at the top left and a taller float at the top right. Lines of text run between them, then under the left float beside the right one. Under a dashed line marked clear: both, a paragraph takes the whole width below both floats.

step.cmd: Float a figure to the top or the bottom of the page

info.p: Set float-reference: page and float the element to an edge of the page area: top, bottom, left or right, or the flow-relative block-start, block-end, inline-start and inline-end. The figure goes to that edge of the page where it is mentioned, and the text of the page goes on in the rest of the page area. Two figures at the same edge stack one after the other. A figure at the top or the bottom is as wide as its content, up to the width of the page area, and stands at the start of the line.

A figure that does not fit on its page goes to the next page. So does a figure whose own mention it would push to the next page. A figure that is larger than a whole page area still goes on a page, at its edge.

float-offset moves the figure away from the edge, and from the figure before it at that edge. A percentage is of the room left beside the figure: float-offset: 50% on a float: left figure centers it across the page.

clear on a page float closes its page to the later figures that go to the edges it names, so clear: top on a figure at the top keeps the next figure for the top of the next page. The footnote area stays at the bottom of the page, under the figures at the bottom.

image.alt: A page with two figures stacked at the top of the page area, one figure at its bottom and one along its left side. The lines of text fill the rest of the page area.

step.cmd: Float a figure to the top or the bottom of a column

info.p: Inside a multi-column element, float-reference: column floats the figure to an edge of the column where it is mentioned, as a page float does in a page. A figure that does not fit goes to the next column. Outside any column, the figure floats beside its lines.

step.cmd: Send a figure to a later page or column

info.p: float-defer moves a page or column float on by a number of pages or columns. A negative number counts back from the last page or column, and last is the last one. CSSMedia lays the document out again until the page each figure goes to stays the same.

step.cmd: Move a figure to an edge only when it is close to it

info.p: snap-block() floats a page or column figure to the top or the bottom only when it stands within the distance you give of that edge. A figure further away stays where it is in the text. Give one distance for both edges, or two for the top and the bottom, and then start, end or near to say where it goes; with near, a figure close to both edges goes to the bottom. snap-block alone is snap-block(2em, near). snap-inline() does the same with the start and the end of the line, with left, right or near. With float-reference: inline, the figure stays in the text.

step.cmd: Wrap the text around a shape

info.p: A float beside its lines takes its whole margin box. shape-outside gives it another outline for the lines: a basic shape such as circle() or polygon(), drawn in the margin box or in the box you name, a box alone such as content-box, or an image such as a url() or a gradient, whose pixels with an alpha above shape-image-threshold make the shape. Each line starts where the shape ends at its height. shape-margin keeps the lines that far from the shape. The shape is cut to the margin box, and the float itself is still placed by its margin box. The lines wrap on one side of the float only.

image.alt: A square float whose upper left half is a shaded triangle. The lines of text beside it start further to the left at each line, along the diagonal of the triangle, until they take the whole width under the float.

info.p: In vertical lines, left and right of a float beside its lines are the top and the bottom, as for text-align. A page or column float goes to the physical edge it names: in vertical-rl, top is where the lines start, right is where the first line is, and the text goes on in the rest. explains writing modes.

result.p: Your figures stand at the edges of their lines, columns or pages, and the text runs around them.
